metrics.|S11| at the measured plane: 0.00610 = -44.29 dB at x = 9.20 mm, the first station: that is the plane the station fit refers its reflection to, because a lumped source's own plane is defined by the gap it drives and not by a coordinate
metrics.|S11| at the port plane: 0.00610 = -44.29 dB after exp(-2j beta d) with d = 4.40 mm: the same reflection moved onto the plane an instrument at the pad would see, and beta is real here, so the move changes phase and nothing else
metrics.|S11| as VSWR: 1.0123 : 1 from (1 + |gamma|) / (1 - |gamma|) with |gamma| = 0.00610: a reflection at this level is easier to read as a mismatch than as a decibel
metrics.|S21| between station planes: 0.990640 = -0.082 dB between x = 9.20 mm and x = 22.00 mm, 12.80 mm apart: one plane at each end, each split into its forward wave and the two divided, so no fit stands between the planes
metrics.passivity bound: |S11|^2 + |S21|^2 betwe: 0.981405 from |S11|^2 = 0.000037 plus |S21|^2 = 0.981367: a passive network must satisfy |S11|^2 + |S21|^2 <= 1, and the two sides of that bound are two different claims.  Above 1 is a bug.  Near 1 is what a model with no material loss should return, because the sum is the power budget of the two station planes and with nothing in the model to absorb energy there is nothing for it to be short of.  Well below 1 is power that left through something the two planes do not see -- an absorbing boundary close enough to the line, a source that radiates -- and that sink has to be found before any number from this run is quoted.  The plain sum is legitimate here because both magnitudes are read on the same cross-section, the two station planes, and the split hands both of them the one zc chosen for this record: the per-plane sqrt(Re zc) weighting is then the same factor on both terms and cancels, where two planes on different cross-sections would need it written out.
